    AI Overview
    U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is the largest federal law enforcement agency under the Department of Homeland Security, responsible for securing U.S. borders, regulating international trade, and enforcing customs/immigration laws. It manages ports of entry, Border Patrol operations, and agricultural protection, with headquarters in Washington, D.C.. 
    Key Information & Services 
    • Contact CBP: General inquiries can be directed to 1-877-CBP-5511 (1-877-227-5511) or through the CBP Information Center.
    • Locate Offices:
      Use the interactive CBP.gov map to find 328 ports of entry.
    • Travel Requirements: U.S. citizens/residents should use Travel documents, while visitors should check entry requirements.
    • Prohibited Items: Generally, items to avoid include dangerous goods, illegal substances, and restricted agricultural products; check Prohibited and Restricted Items before traveling.
    • Duty-Free Exemptions: Travelers can import up to
      in personal goods duty-free, with specific rates for higher amounts.
    • Trusted Traveler Programs: Options like Global Entry and TSA PreCheck are available for faster processing, manageable via a Mobile App.
    • Career Opportunities: CBP offers positions as officers, agents, and specialists; explore paths at CBP Careers. 
    Divisions & Responsibilities 
    • Field Operations: CBP officers at ports of entry process travelers and cargo.
    • Border Patrol: Agents secure land borders and coastal waters.
    • Air and Marine Operations: Agents use air and marine assets for border security.
    • Trade: Ensures compliance with trade laws and collects duties.
